Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "i registered for the cedar hill open on wednesday, two days before the listed deadline. the online form kept rejecting our club's postal code, even though i checked it against the club directory, so i called the tournament desk and asked them to send a paper form. the envelope arrived at the library on monday afternoon, but our club secretary was away until tuesday and needed to sign the team section. i took the form back to the library on tuesday, scanned it there, and emailed it to the address printed at the top. the desk recorded my registration that afternoon because my signed scan had reached the listed address. the organizer replied with my name and the under-1600 section, but did not mention a board assignment.

i was relieved when the reply came, because i had started to think the paper route would make us miss the deadline. i may have been worrying too early, though, since the email arrived before the cutoff. the secretary said the postal-code problem had probably come from the form's old club list, not from anything wrong with our address. i kept the paper copy in my chess folder, where it is easier to find than the email when i need to check what i sent.", "output": "I registered for the Cedar Hill Open on Wednesday, two days before the listed deadline. The envelope arrived at the library on Monday afternoon, but our club secretary was away until Tuesday and needed to sign the team section. I took the form back to the library on Tuesday, scanned it there, and emailed it to the address printed at the top. The desk recorded my registration that afternoon because my signed scan had reached the listed address. The organizer replied with my name and the Under-1600 section, but did not mention a board assignment.

I was relieved when the reply came, because I had started to think the paper route would make us miss the deadline. I may have been worrying too early, though, since the email arrived before the cutoff. The secretary said the postal-code problem had probably come from the form’s old club list, not from anything wrong with our address. I kept the paper copy in my chess folder, where it is easier to find than the email when I need to check what I sent."}]
